title: Marine & Transport
summary: Shipping companies use PI System for whole-ship monitoring, fuel and emissions tracking, predictive maintenance and crew training. Vessels buffer data onboard and send critical data ashore by satellite, with non-critical data uploaded later.
hierarchy:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  FL[Fleet] --> V[Vessel]
  V --> S1[Main Engine]
  V --> S2[Auxiliary Engines and Gensets]
  V --> S3[Boilers and Thermal Oil]
  V --> S4[Hull]
  V --> S5[Cranes and Self-unloader]
  V --> S6[Navigation]
  S1 --> C1[Cylinder 1 to n]
```

kpis.name: Upload bandwidth
kpis.definition: Ship-to-shore data volume; CSL reported up to 50% reduction.

pitfalls: Limited, unreliable bandwidth needs prioritised critical and non-critical data paths (CSL).
Frequent crew turnover causes inconsistent data (CSL).
Onboard data silos prevent learning across the fleet (Caterpillar).
Weather and ocean conditions add "noise" to operational data (Caterpillar).
verifyNote: The vessel AF hierarchy, Vessel template and carbon intensity expression are inferred. IMO CII/EEXI and EU MRV reporting with PI, and rail and port PI cases, were not found in a readable source.
